You have superpowers.

**Below is the full content of your 'superpowers:using-superpowers' skill - your introduction to using skills. For all other skills, use the 'Skill' tool:**

---
name: using-superpowers
description: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
---

<SUBAGENT-STOP>
If you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, ignore this skill.
</SUBAGENT-STOP>

<EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>
If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.

IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

This is not negotiable. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven't already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.

Then announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]" and follow the skill exactly. If it has a checklist, create a todo per item.

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## Platform Adaptation

If your harness appears here, read its reference file for special instructions:

- Claude Code: `references/claude-code-tools.md`
- Codex: `references/codex-tools.md`
- Pi: `references/pi-tools.md`
- Antigravity: `references/antigravity-tools.md`
- Hermes Agent: `references/hermes-tools.md`
- Muse: `references/muse-tools.md`

## User Instructions

User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior. Only skip skill workflows or instructions when your human partner has explicitly told you to.
</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>"
  }
}

commands.name: hyperframes
commands.description: Mandatory entry point: read this first for any request to make, create, edit, animate, or render a video, animation, or motion graphic, including a promo, explainer, captioned clip, title card, overlay, slideshow or interactive deck, Remotion port, or any HyperFrames HTML composition. Also use it to inspect, diagnose, validate, preview, publish, or batch-render an existing HyperFrames project. Inputs may be a website URL, GitHub PR, Figma design or URL, text or brief, existing footage, or music. It resumes project state, captures intent when applicable, selects and installs the owning workflow, and routes domain capabilities. HyperFrames is the default output framework unless the user explicitly chooses another framework for the deliverable or asks only to record a browser session. (user)

commands.name: hyperframes-animation
commands.description: All animation knowledge for HyperFrames — atomic motion rules, multi-phase scene blueprints, scene transitions, broader motion-design techniques, AND the seven runtime adapters (GSAP default, plus Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS keyframes, Web Animations API, TypeGPU). Use for any motion or animation task: pick 2-4 rules and compose, or load a blueprint, or look up runtime-specific API (e.g. GSAP eases / Lottie player / Three.js mixer). Also covers auditing an existing composition's choreography (animation map) and 24 named text-animation effects. HyperFrames-native: single paused timeline, seek-safe, deterministic. (user)

commands.name: hyperframes-audio
commands.description: Use when audio already placed in a HyperFrames composition needs to be mixed: fade-in/fade-out, crossfade, track gain or volume, volume automation, ducking, a music bed that fights a voiceover (voiceover carve), effects on a track (EQ, compressor, limiter, gate, saturation, delay, reverb, chorus, phaser, bitcrush), automation envelopes drawn on a track's volume or any effect parameter, or one submix bus carrying a chain, a fader and an automation clock for several tracks at once (`<hf-audio-group>`). Don't use for sourcing or generating audio — finding BGM, SFX, or making a voiceover is `/media-use`. Don't use for clip timing or track layout, which is `/hyperframes-core`. (user)

commands.name: hyperframes-cli
commands.description: Use the HyperFrames CLI development loop: init, add, catalog, capture, lint, check, snapshot, compare, grade-compare, preview, play, present, beats, keyframes, single or batch render, publish, cloud, cloudrun, feedback, lambda, doctor, browser, info, upgrade, skills, compositions, timeline, history, clean, docs, benchmark, telemetry, transcribe, auth, tts, and remove-background. Also use when diagnosing build or render failures. validate, inspect, and layout are deprecated aliases; use check. Covers local, HeyGen-hosted cloud, AWS Lambda, and Google Cloud Run rendering. (user)

commands.name: hyperframes-core
commands.description: The HyperFrames composition contract — build one renderable project. Use for composition structure, the `data-*` timing attributes, `class="clip"`, tracks, sub-compositions, variables, framework-owned media playback, deterministic-render rules, and validation. Read before writing composition HTML. (user)

commands.name: hyperframes-creative
commands.description: Non-animation creative direction for HyperFrames videos. Use for design spec (frame.md / design.md) handling, palettes, typography, narration, beat planning, audio-reactive visuals, composition patterns, and brand / style decisions. For atomic motion patterns and scene blueprints, use `hyperframes-animation`. (user)

commands.name: hyperframes-keyframes
commands.description: Use when a HyperFrames composition needs a punch-in, punch-out, zoom, reframe, Ken Burns treatment, camera move, visual match/whip handoff, or other seek-safe 2D/3D keyframes; also for GSAP, CSS keyframes, Anime.js, WAAPI, FLIP, paths, masks, SVG morph/draw, text trails, 3D depth, or `hyperframes keyframes` diagnostics. Don't use for broad scene strategy, brand design, media sourcing, captions, or general video planning. (user)

commands.name: hyperframes-registry
commands.description: Search, install, and wire registry blocks and components into HyperFrames compositions. Use BEFORE hand-building any named visual — whenever a brief, a user, or a storyboard names a look, effect, treatment, or transition such as CRT scanlines, glitch, chromatic aberration, film grain, a shimmer sweep, a chart, a code or terminal window, a map, or a confetti burst — because roughly 400 hosted items already cover many of them and the search ranks all of them with nothing installed, no project, and no account. Also use when running hyperframes add or hyperframes catalog, installing one item or every block matching a tag, wiring an installed item into index.html, or working with hyperframes.json. Covers discovery, install locations, block sub-composition wiring, component snippet merging, and authoring a new block or component to contribute upstream (idea → scaffold → validate → PR). (user)

commands.name: hyperframes-studio
commands.description: Use when working with a person on a HyperFrames project in Studio: first, whether their message asks for a change at all (questions, loose ideas and "don't change anything" get an answer and a plan, not an edit); for a new film, the plan, storyboard and build order that the HyperFrames launch films follow; and how the timeline should be laid out so it reads well (one caption track, one element kind per track, every scene a sub-composition) and where captions and key content may sit (safe zones). Don't use for how to perform an individual edit (split, trim, retime, volume, copy, swap): that is `creator-editing-recipes.md` in `/hyperframes-core`. (user)

commands.name: media-use
commands.description: Agent Media OS for a HyperFrames project. Resolve BGM, SFX, image, icon, brand logo, voice, color grade, or LUT into a frozen local file or paste-ready block + ledger record (one verb, `resolve`); generate via TTS / music / image models when the catalog misses; produce voiceover, transcription, captions, and background removal through one shared audio engine; operate on media (cut / reframe / transform); and reuse assets across projects. Also use for vague feedback that real footage looks dark, flat, boring, should feel retro/camcorder/print/ASCII, needs privacy, or needs a media reveal. When the host app provides its own music or sound-effect tools, use those for music and sound effects; `resolve --type bgm|sfx` needs the heygen CLI. When `HEYGEN_API_BASE` is set, HeyGen calls go through that host with no CLI sign-in. (user)

commands.name: startup-hook-skill
commands.description: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code cloud sessions. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for cloud sessions, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during cloud sessions. (user)

commands.name: agentoon-3d
commands.description: Blender and 3D production for Agentoon.ai: object animation, cinematic lighting, camera paths, depth of field, material animation, environment effects, product visualisation and architectural walkthroughs rendered headless with bpy. Use only when form, space or depth is the subject; not for screen tutorials. (project)

commands.name: agentoon-3d-motion
commands.description: Agentoon.ai real 3D motion (three.js + react-three-fiber via @remotion/three, optional Blender): extruded 3D logos built from the real SVG, 3D extruded text, cinematic camera fly-through along a spline past floating interface panels (real screenshots), fog depth, key/rim/fill lighting, speed ramp, and a Blender turntable pipeline. Use for product/logo hero moments and camera moves through UI. Type /agentoon-3d-motion. (project)

commands.name: agentoon-3d-showcase
commands.description: Agentoon.ai real 3D showcase (three.js + react-three-fiber via @remotion/three, optional Blender): turns a static software logo (SVG) into a rotating extruded 3D object with a cinematic camera ORBIT, floating interface panels (real screenshots) circling at different depths, fog depth and dynamic coloured lights. Type /agentoon-3d-showcase <logo.svg>. (project)

commands.name: agentoon-audio
commands.description: Professional sound direction for Agentoon.ai videos: English voiceover timing and pace, music ducking, subtle keyboard and mouse-click effects, clean dialogue, loudness consistency (-15 LUFS), caption synchronisation. Use for narration generation, mixing, SFX cues and audio QC. (project)

commands.name: agentoon-camera
commands.description: Cinematic camera choreography for Agentoon.ai videos: dolly in/out, tracking, whip pan, orbit, parallax, push-in, rack-focus simulation, tilt, dynamic framing and controlled speed ramps. Use for hero reveals, 3D or footage shots, UI zooms and scene-to-scene camera moves. (project)
commands.argumentHint: <shot or scene to move the camera on>

commands.name: agentoon-carousel
commands.description: Build a complete Agentoon.ai Instagram carousel from any AI topic, e.g. `/agentoon-carousel How MCP servers work`. Researches official docs, writes the slides, designs fresh layouts and illustrations for that topic, renders 7–9 static 1080×1350 PNGs with Playwright, runs a quality gate (mobile size, contrast, overflow, spelling), and delivers PNGs + contact sheet + editable source + ZIP + SEO caption. Use for any Agentoon.ai carousel, or "make a carousel about X". (project)

commands.name: agentoon-cinematic-cuts
commands.description: Agentoon.ai Remotion cut between two ordinary video scenes: camera-driven push toward a target point in scene A, a motion-matched cut where scene B starts at the same zoom with its target on the same screen point, circular mask transition and real sub-frame motion blur, then a matched zoom-out. Replaces a hard cut with a meaningful transition. Type /agentoon-cinematic-cuts <a.mp4> <b.mp4>. (project)

commands.name: agentoon-cinematic-fx
commands.description: Agentoon.ai cinematic Remotion tools: scene transitions (circle reveal / match cut, diagonal mask wipe, depth push, whip with motion blur), camera motion blur, tracking camera rig with lag, depth-of-field parallax layers, one-shot light sweep, and controlled speed ramps. Use to connect scenes and direct attention. Type /agentoon-cinematic-fx. (project)

commands.name: agentoon-data-flow
commands.description: Agentoon.ai Remotion technical explainer for MCP and AI-agent workflows: static workflow becomes nodes appearing in sequence, animated connection lines, labelled data packets moving along the lines, and a highlighted API path. Type /agentoon-data-flow <workflow description>. (Components shared with /agentoon-infographics.) (project)
commands.argumentHint: <nodes and edges, e.g. "Claude -> MCP server -> GitHub, Files">

commands.name: agentoon-data-motion
commands.description: Agentoon.ai Remotion data-motion components: animated counters (0 to 1,000), rolling digits / odometer, percentage roll (0 to 95%), progress bars, circular progress, countdown timers, animated bar and line charts, all frame-based so numbers land on narrated cues. Use for statistics, results, comparisons of numbers, "N tools / N% / N seconds" beats. Type /agentoon-data-motion. (project)

commands.name: agentoon-diagrams
commands.description: Technical storytelling diagrams for Agentoon.ai: MCP connection diagrams, animated data flows, API request/response visualisations, agent-to-agent communication, node graphs, network diagrams, workflow timelines. Use to explain how systems connect; every diagram is labelled as a diagram and never stands in as proof of a real connection. (project)
commands.argumentHint: <systems to connect and what flows between them>

commands.name: agentoon-director
commands.description: Master creative director for Agentoon.ai videos. Use FIRST on any new reel, tutorial, explainer or transformation video, e.g. `/agentoon-director How to connect Claude to Bland with MCP`. Analyses the topic, footage and narration, picks only the specialist skills (motion, camera, typography, robot, ui, 3d, morph, diagrams, audio, transitions, qc) that serve the story, and writes a scene-by-scene plan with a visual identity that differs from earlier episodes. (project)
commands.argumentHint: <topic or brief, optionally a reference video path>

commands.name: agentoon-infographics
commands.description: Agentoon.ai Remotion animated diagrams: MCP/API connection diagrams with flowing data dots along bezier lines, node networks, timelines, process steps, morphing software comparison cards, animated arrows and callouts. Use to explain how systems connect, step order, or compare two tools. Type /agentoon-infographics. (project)

commands.name: agentoon-kinetic-type
commands.description: Agentoon.ai Remotion kinetic typography: spring word reveals, character-by-character flip-up reveals, text morphing between two strings, marker word highlighting, extruded 3D titles, and word-timed animated subtitles. Use for key points, hooks, quotes, "before/after" wording, captions. Type /agentoon-kinetic-type. (project)

commands.name: agentoon-logo-motion
commands.description: Agentoon.ai Remotion logo animation on REAL logo assets: scale/blur/mask reveal with ring burst, particle reveal built from the logo's own pixels, shape morphing that lands on the logo, product-style 3D-tilt presentation with reflection, and logo-to-logo transitions. For true 3D logos use /agentoon-3d-motion. Use for software introductions in tutorials and roundups. Type /agentoon-logo-motion. (project)

commands.name: agentoon-morph
commands.description: Before-and-after and transformation reveals for Agentoon.ai: comparison sliders, image wipes, mask reveals, shape morphing, match cuts, split screens, image expansion. Use when demonstrating a real tool's result (image edits, restores, clean-ups, upgrades). Requires genuine before and after assets. (project)
commands.argumentHint: <what changes, and where the real before/after files are>

commands.name: agentoon-motion
commands.description: Professional motion graphics for Agentoon.ai videos: kinetic animation, easing, spring motion, staggered reveals, layered depth, motion blur, animated cards and floating UI. Use when scenes need cards, lists, steps or UI chrome to feel alive; not for camera moves (/agentoon-camera) or text (/agentoon-typography). (project)

commands.name: agentoon-number-motion
commands.description: Agentoon.ai Remotion number animation for static statistics: counter 0 to 1,000, rolling odometer 0% to 95%, animated progress ring, moving bar chart and spring-based numeric transitions, all frame-driven with exact end values. Type /agentoon-number-motion <stats>. (Components shared with /agentoon-data-motion.) (project)

commands.name: agentoon-qc
commands.description: Final production review for Agentoon.ai videos. Audits software authenticity, logos, readability, narration accuracy, robot lip-sync, animation smoothness, placeholders, fake results, aspect ratio, audio and mobile-safe captions; writes QC-REPORT.md and blocks FINAL status when major errors remain. Use before delivering any preview or final MP4. (project)
commands.argumentHint: <path to the episode folder or MP4>

commands.name: agentoon-robot
commands.description: The original Agentoon.ai presenter robot. Reuse the approved character with narration-synced lip movement, blinking, head and gesture acting, pointing at software or connector controls, reactions to results, camera-facing delivery and the signature ending. Never redesigns the robot. (project)

commands.name: agentoon-transitions
commands.description: Professional scene transitions for Agentoon.ai: match cut, mask wipe, whip pan, zoom-through, depth transition, motion-matched cut, seamless object transition, camera-driven and exposure-based transitions, chosen by narrative purpose and never overused. Use when planning or building the cuts between scenes. (project)

commands.name: agentoon-typography
commands.description: Premium animated text for Agentoon.ai videos: kinetic typography, word-by-word captions synced to narration, phrase highlighting, masked reveals, tracking, animated numbers, title cards and emphasis. commands.name: hyperframes:hyperframes
commands.description: (hyperframes) Mandatory entry point: read this first for any request to make, create, edit, animate, or render a video, animation, or motion graphic, including a promo, explainer, captioned clip, title card, overlay, slideshow or interactive deck, Remotion port, or any HyperFrames HTML composition. Also use it to inspect, diagnose, validate, preview, publish, or batch-render an existing HyperFrames project. Inputs may be a website URL, GitHub PR, Figma design or URL, text or brief, existing footage, or music. It resumes project state, captures intent when applicable, selects and installs the owning workflow, and routes domain capabilities. HyperFrames is the default output framework unless the user explicitly chooses another framework for the deliverable or asks only to record a browser session.

commands.name: hyperframes:hyperframes-animation
commands.description: (hyperframes) All animation knowledge for HyperFrames — atomic motion rules, multi-phase scene blueprints, scene transitions, broader motion-design techniques, AND the seven runtime adapters (GSAP default, plus Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS keyframes, Web Animations API, TypeGPU). Use for any motion or animation task: pick 2-4 rules and compose, or load a blueprint, or look up runtime-specific API (e.g. GSAP eases / Lottie player / Three.js mixer). Also covers auditing an existing composition's choreography (animation map) and 24 named text-animation effects. HyperFrames-native: single paused timeline, seek-safe, deterministic.

commands.name: hyperframes:hyperframes-audio
commands.description: (hyperframes) Use when audio already placed in a HyperFrames composition needs to be mixed: fade-in/fade-out, crossfade, track gain or volume, volume automation, ducking, a music bed that fights a voiceover (voiceover carve), effects on a track (EQ, compressor, limiter, gate, saturation, delay, reverb, chorus, phaser, bitcrush), automation envelopes drawn on a track's volume or any effect parameter, or one submix bus carrying a chain, a fader and an automation clock for several tracks at once (`<hf-audio-group>`). Don't use for sourcing or generating audio — finding BGM, SFX, or making a voiceover is `/media-use`. Don't use for clip timing or track layout, which is `/hyperframes-core`.

commands.name: hyperframes:hyperframes-cli
commands.description: (hyperframes) Use the HyperFrames CLI development loop: init, add, catalog, capture, lint, check, snapshot, compare, grade-compare, preview, play, present, beats, keyframes, single or batch render, publish, cloud, cloudrun, feedback, lambda, doctor, browser, info, upgrade, skills, compositions, timeline, history, clean, docs, benchmark, telemetry, transcribe, auth, tts, and remove-background. Also use when diagnosing build or render failures. validate, inspect, and layout are deprecated aliases; use check. Covers local, HeyGen-hosted cloud, AWS Lambda, and Google Cloud Run rendering.

commands.name: hyperframes:hyperframes-core
commands.description: (hyperframes) The HyperFrames composition contract — build one renderable project. Use for composition structure, the `data-*` timing attributes, `class="clip"`, tracks, sub-compositions, variables, framework-owned media playback, deterministic-render rules, and validation. Read before writing composition HTML.

commands.name: hyperframes:hyperframes-creative
commands.description: (hyperframes) Non-animation creative direction for HyperFrames videos. Use for design spec (frame.md / design.md) handling, palettes, typography, narration, beat planning, audio-reactive visuals, composition patterns, and brand / style decisions. For atomic motion patterns and scene blueprints, use `hyperframes-animation`.

commands.name: hyperframes:hyperframes-keyframes
commands.description: (hyperframes) Use when a HyperFrames composition needs a punch-in, punch-out, zoom, reframe, Ken Burns treatment, camera move, visual match/whip handoff, or other seek-safe 2D/3D keyframes; also for GSAP, CSS keyframes, Anime.js, WAAPI, FLIP, paths, masks, SVG morph/draw, text trails, 3D depth, or `hyperframes keyframes` diagnostics. Don't use for broad scene strategy, brand design, media sourcing, captions, or general video planning.

commands.name: hyperframes:hyperframes-registry

Use BEFORE hand-building any named visual — whenever a brief, a user, or a storyboard names a look, effect, treatment, or transition such as CRT scanlines, glitch, chromatic aberration, film grain, a shimmer sweep, a chart, a code or terminal window, a map, or a confetti burst — because roughly 400 hosted items already cover many of them and the search ranks all of them with nothing installed, no project, and no account. Also use when running hyperframes add or hyperframes catalog, installing one item or every block matching a tag, wiring an installed item into index.html, or working with hyperframes.json. Covers discovery, install locations, block sub-composition wiring, component snippet merging, and authoring a new block or component to contribute upstream (idea → scaffold → validate → PR).

commands.name: hyperframes:hyperframes-studio
commands.description: (hyperframes) Use when working with a person on a HyperFrames project in Studio: first, whether their message asks for a change at all (questions, loose ideas and "don't change anything" get an answer and a plan, not an edit); for a new film, the plan, storyboard and build order that the HyperFrames launch films follow; and how the timeline should be laid out so it reads well (one caption track, one element kind per track, every scene a sub-composition) and where captions and key content may sit (safe zones). Don't use for how to perform an individual edit (split, trim, retime, volume, copy, swap): that is `creator-editing-recipes.md` in `/hyperframes-core`.

commands.name: hyperframes:media-use

Resolve BGM, SFX, image, icon, brand logo, voice, color grade, or LUT into a frozen local file or paste-ready block + ledger record (one verb, `resolve`); generate via TTS / music / image models when the catalog misses; produce voiceover, transcription, captions, and background removal through one shared audio engine; operate on media (cut / reframe / transform); and reuse assets across projects. Also use for vague feedback that real footage looks dark, flat, boring, should feel retro/camcorder/print/ASCII, needs privacy, or needs a media reveal. Cites the source platform on every figure. Does not recommend funds, forecast NAVs/IRRs, or simulate allocation changes. Triggers on "alts brief", "/alts-brief", "prep the [client]'s alts review", "what's going on with [client]'s PE/private investments", "how's [client] doing on their alts", or any request to review a household's alternative investment positions before a meeting.

Produces a fail/flag/note markup, required disclosures, a books-and-records scratch-pad entry, and an archiving handoff reminder. Triggers on "compliance check", "/compliance", "is this compliant", "review this before I send it", "can I say this to a client", "check this email/post/deck". Use it whenever an advisor asks to check, review, or look over anything before it goes to a client or prospect — "check this before I send it", "look this over before it goes out" — even a routine note, because deciding that a message needs no changes is part of the review, not a reason to skip it.

commands.name: claude-for-financial-advisors:estate-and-tax-brief

The only write is optional advisor-approved CRM follow-up tasks, shown for approval first. Never drafts trust language, gives legal advice, retitles an account or changes a beneficiary. Triggers on "estate brief", "estate meeting brief", "estate and tax brief", "estate plan review for [client]", "check [client]'s trust funding", "are [client]'s beneficiaries up to date", or "does [client]'s estate plan match their accounts".
